title: On the Statistical Mechanics of Attention
authors: Jerry Yao-Chieh Hu, Yu-An Chen, Maojiang Su, Han Liu
abstract: We revisit the statistical mechanics of Transformer attention via modern Hopfield models. We present a free-energy formalism to characterize parameter regimes and critical thresholds for robust attention inference. The resulting free-energy landscape incorporates randomness in query states and attention weights. Attention then emerges as the equation of motion of the corresponding statistical-mechanical system (i.e., modern Hopfield model) through the standard free-energy minimization principle. This allows us to identify first-order phase transitions in attention between glassy and robust-inference phases. We further extend to attentions with stochastic queries and keys. Together, our results provide a rigorous statistical-mechanics framework for characterizing phase structure and inference reliability across a family of Transformer attention mechanisms.
summary: This paper develops a statistical mechanics framework to analyze Transformer attention by mapping it onto a Modern Hopfield Model. Using a free-energy formalism derived from Tsallis entropy, the authors characterize the phase structure, revealing distinct transitions between reliable and glassy inference regimes. This provides a fundamental physical understanding of attention's computational reliability.
main_problem: The paper aims to rigorously characterize the statistical mechanics of the Transformer attention mechanism to understand its parameter regimes and critical thresholds for reliable inference.
main_result: Attention is shown to emerge naturally as the equation of motion derived from minimizing a free-energy functional, allowing for the identification of first-order phase transitions between glassy and robust-inference states.
method: The authors employ a free-energy formalism, connecting it to Tsallis entropy ($\Psi_\alpha$), and modeling the system using modern Hopfield models (MHM).
model_or_system: The system is the Transformer attention mechanism, mathematically mapped onto a Modern Hopfield Model (MHM) defined by a joint energy function. The analysis extends to stochastic queries and keys.
key_observables: Free-energy landscape ($\Gamma_\alpha$), attention weights, phase structure (glassy vs. robust-inference), and critical thresholds.
important_parameters: The Tsallis entropy index ($\alpha$), the memory load ($\kappa$), and the inverse temperature ($ eta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis initially focuses on the deterministic regime (zero variance) but provides a framework to extend to fluctuations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the procedure from microscopic fluctuations to the macroscopic energy landscape via Fenchel-Young duality, and numerical results validate theoretical formulas for coexistence and spinodal points.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the physical formulation via MHM, deriving the free-energy landscape, analyzing the resulting phase transitions, and concluding with numerical validations of the theoretical predictions.
why_interesting: The rigorous application of concepts from spin-glass theory (Hopfield models, free energy minimization) to a core component of modern AI (Transformers) provides a deep physical understanding of AI reliability.
